decision.rationale: Promote. The frozen candidate is a structurally extended version of the incumbent ('paced bus plus per-bank row/occupancy state': conditional precharge, bank busy-until, column-command pacing, same bus-slot/queue-scale frame) and it improves the first primary objective, core-cycle accuracy, broadly: case-mean absolute core error 7.56% -> 3.41% on the named training cohort (-4.15 pp, -54.9% relative; 13/14 cases better; worst case 19.57% -> 12.12%) and 9.91% -> 6.36% on the anonymized validation group (-3.55 pp, -35.8%; 10/14 better; worst case 49.87% -> 44.71%; excluding the two dominant failure cases val3/val7, 4.99% -> 2.14%). On the second primary objective the two groups disagree: validation MAE/L improves 0.2441 -> 0.2195 (-10.1%, 11/14 cases) while training MAE/L regresses 0.2407 -> 0.2786 (+15.8%, 6/14 cases, concentrated in conflict-heavy workloads); net over all 28 cases request MAE is approximately flat (+0.007 absolute, ~+3%). Signed bias improves in both groups (|drift|/L 0.125 -> 0.061 training, 0.158 -> 0.069 validation), replacing the incumbent's near-one-sided underprediction (13/14 training cases negative) with mixed-sign residuals, and the largest individual failures shrink (val7 28.97% -> 18.74%, val2 7.06% -> 0.39%, val8 10.23% -> 5.63%, val14 12.47% -> 6.68%, gap_sssp 19.57% -> 12.03%). Against the stage-entry reference the candidate is better on every mean except the p99.9 tail (core 23.67% -> 3.41% / 24.90% -> 6.36%; MAE 0.543 -> 0.279 / 0.531 -> 0.220; |bias| ~0.54 -> 0.06/0.07; p99.9/L 4.38 -> 5.43 / 3.49 -> 4.60). The decisive costs, recorded honestly below, are (i) tails worse on both splits versus both references and (ii) the training-cohort MAE regression. I accept them because they are secondary to the stated primary objectives, affect ~1% of reads at p99 and 0.19% beyond 5L, and the new positive overshoot magnitudes are of the same order as the incumbent's existing negative outliers (-1800 to -2245 cycles). Coverage and mechanical identities rule out coverage/sample artifacts, and the core gain is not mere cancellation: |bias| and validation MAE improve alongside the signed core metric; where core improves while MAE worsens (arizona/bravo/cactu/charlie/lbm) the change is a bias-variance trade, which I flag as residual risk. Remaining single-core failures (val3 44.7%, val7 18.7%, training gap_* ~12%) are reduced, not fixed. Under the contract's priority ordering the improvement is substantial, consistent and mechanism-plausible; no contract violation was demonstrated. If the secondary p99/p99.9 tails were weighted at primary-objective level, this trade could go the other way.
